patch_description: Replace the single shuffled greedy pass with repeated randomized erosion passes that stop when deletions have become unproductive. A cell that was not removable early in a pass may become removable after nearby cells are deleted, so revisiting cells can improve the initial zero region substantially. Conversely, several consecutive zero-yield blocks indicate that greedy erosion is exhausted; stopping then preserves the remaining budget for simulated annealing, where non-monotone restructuring is more valuable.
